title: Verified false-positive evidence: domains removed from catalystprimeagent-bot/disposable-email-domains
purpose: Most disposable-email-domain aggregators (including this one, until 2026-10-05) ultimately derive from the same handful of upstream lists. One of them, disposable/disposable, maintains a hand-curated whitelist.txt of domains its maintainers manually reviewed and removed as wrongly classified. This file re-verifies each of those domains independently tonight -- live DNS (MX/A) and a live HTTP fetch where one exists -- rather than repeating the upstream claim unchecked. It exists so other list maintainers can consume machine-readable, per-domain evidence directly, instead of taking our word (or disposable/disposable's) on faith. See README.md for how this file is produced and used.
methodology: For each domain: `dig MX` and `dig A` against the system resolver, and (if any A record resolved) a 5s HTTPS GET for status code and <title>. No WHOIS lookup was available in this run (tool not installed), so domain age is not claimed anywhere in this file. Where evidence was weak or absent, confidence is marked 'medium', 'low', or 'none' rather than omitting the entry or rounding it up to 'high' -- a prior PR to a different project overclaimed a safeguard that did not hold up under a maintainer's scrutiny, and this file is built specifically not to repeat that. Entries added 2026-10-09 come from a different route and say so in `provenance`: a stratified random-sample audit of our OWN published list (see audit/README.md), where the evidence is live DNS-over-HTTPS (MX/A/TXT/_dmarc) plus an HTTP root fetch recorded at audit time. Only verdicts at confidence 'high' -- meaning both a live web root naming a real-world organisation AND mail hosting that is paid per mailbox or an enterprise gateway -- were promoted here and removed from the list. The audit's medium-confidence findings are deliberately NOT in this file and are NOT excluded from the list; they are reported as an upper band instead.
upstream_whitelist_full_set_note: disposable/disposable's whitelist.txt lists 39 domains in total; this file independently re-verifies the 16 that were confirmed present in our own published list before commit 65f52ab (2026-10-05). The other 23 are excluded from our build (see scripts/update.py EXCLUSIONS) on the upstream source alone and are not yet independently checked here -- they are not included in this evidence file until they are.
